steps.note: If an INVALID orders_customer_id_idx is left over from an interrupted concurrent build, rename it out of the way (IF NOT EXISTS below would otherwise skip and leave an unusable index). A valid one is left alone.
steps.sql: DO $$ BEGIN IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_index i JOIN pg_class c ON c.oid = i.indexrelid JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = c.relnamespace WHERE n.nspname = 'public' AND c.relname = 'orders_customer_id_idx' AND NOT i.indisvalid) THEN ALTER INDEX public.orders_customer_id_idx RENAME TO orders_customer_id_idx_invalid; END IF; END $$;

steps.note: Drop the leftover invalid index, if any, without blocking reads or writes. Alone in its step: CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction block.
steps.sql: DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS public.orders_customer_id_idx_invalid;

steps.note: Build the index concurrently: only a SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE lock, so the app's inserts and reads (2 s timeout) keep running during the build on 10M rows. Alone in its step for the same reason.
steps.sql: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS orders_customer_id_idx ON public.orders (customer_id);

steps.note: Verify the index exists and is valid; fail the plan loudly otherwise.
steps.sql: DO $$ BEGIN IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_index i JOIN pg_class c ON c.oid = i.indexrelid JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = c.relnamespace WHERE n.nspname = 'public' AND c.relname = 'orders_customer_id_idx' AND i.indrelid = 'public.orders'::regclass AND i.indisvalid AND i.indisready) THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'orders_customer_id_idx is missing or invalid'; END IF; END $$;
